records.source: בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית בָּרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: In beginning created God the heavens and the earth.
pieces: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

L.1: In [the] beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

R.1: In the beginning, God created everything: the heavens and the earth.

decisions.choice: In the beginning: a statement that stands on its own and opens the account
alternatives: When God began to create the heavens and the earth (a time clause that leads into verse 2 or 3)
decisions.reason: The word for beginning has no article, and the verse could be read as leading into what follows: "When God began to create the heavens and the earth, the earth was formless...". The second account opens in a similar way (2:4: "in the day that the LORD God made..."). But the Masoretic accents mark a pause after the first word, so that it reads as complete in itself, and the Septuagint, the oldest translation, reads the verse as a main clause, as John 1:1 echoes it. Read either way, God is there and acting before anything else is described.

decisions.choice: created: a verb that the Bible uses only with God as the one who acts
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament this verb is used only of what God does, and it never names a material that something is made from. Genesis 1 uses it at three points: for the heavens and the earth (verse 1), for the first living creatures (verse 21) and for human beings (verse 27, three times). The chapter also uses everyday verbs such as "made" for God's work, so this verb alone does not settle how God created; but the opening verse places God before and above everything that exists.

decisions.choice: God: the one God, though the word is plural in form
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form and in other places can mean "gods" (Exodus 20:3). Here its verb is singular, "he created", as it is throughout the chapter, so it names the one God. Hebrew often uses a plural form to express greatness or fullness.

decisions.choice: the heavens and the earth: everything that exists
alternatives: the sky and the land, and nothing more
decisions.reason: Naming two opposite ends to mean everything between them is a common way of speaking in Hebrew. "The heavens and the earth" is the whole ordered world, from the sky above to the ground below; Hebrew has no single word for the universe. The account closes with the same words (2:1).

decisions.choice: In [the] beginning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no article here (meaning decision m1); English needs one, so Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: everything: the heavens and the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair of words means (m4) and keeps the words themselves.

records.heading: God creates the heavens and the earth

records.source: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֨הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And the earth was formlessness and emptiness, and darkness [was] over [the] face of [the] deep, and [the] spirit of God [was] hovering over [the] face of the waters.
pieces: The earth was without form and empty. Darkness lay over the surface of the deep, while the Spirit of God hovered above the waters.

L.2: And the earth was formlessness and emptiness, and darkness [was] over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God [was] hovering over the face of the waters.

R.2: The earth did not have any shape yet, and it was empty. It was dark over the deep water, and the Spirit of God was moving above the water.

decisions.choice: Now the earth was: a description of how things stood, not the next event
alternatives: And the earth became formless and empty (a ruin after an earlier creation)
decisions.reason: The verse puts "the earth" before its verb, a Hebrew way of pausing the story to describe a scene. It tells how things were when God first spoke in verse 3. The verb "was" describes a state here, as it does in 3:1 ("the serpent was more cunning"); it does not say that the earth became formless after an earlier creation.

decisions.choice: formless and empty: not yet ordered and not yet filled
decisions.reason: The two words rhyme in Hebrew. The first is used for a trackless wasteland (Deuteronomy 32:10) and for what is empty or useless; the second appears only with the first (Isaiah 34:11; Jeremiah 4:23, which looks back to this verse). The rest of the chapter answers both: on days one to three God gives the world its form, and on days four to six he fills it.

decisions.choice: the deep: the deep waters that covered the earth
decisions.reason: The word means the waters of the deep sea and the springs beneath the earth (7:11; Psalm 104:6). Here it is the water that covers everything before God separates the waters and the dry land appears (verses 6-10). In this account the deep is not a power that opposes God; it is water, waiting for his word.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. With "God" it could mean a very great wind, since Hebrew sometimes uses "of God" to mean "mighty", and God sends a wind over the waters after the flood (8:1). But elsewhere "the spirit of God" is God's own Spirit at work (Exodus 31:3; 1 Samuel 10:10), and the verb "hovering" (m5) suits a living presence better than a wind. Psalm 33:6 links God's word and his breath in the making of the heavens.

decisions.choice: hovering: moving above, as a bird does over its young
decisions.reason: The same rare verb describes an eagle hovering over its young in Deuteronomy 32:11. It pictures God's presence over the waters, ready to bring order and life.

decisions.choice: the face of (L); the surface of, then simply the waters (B); over the deep water (R)
alternatives: the face of the deep ... the face of the waters
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "face", the Hebrew way of saying "surface", both times. Balanced says "surface" once and lets "the waters" stand alone the second time; Readable says "deep water" for the deep.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים יְהִ֣י א֑וֹר וַֽיְהִי־אֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And said God, let be light, and was light.
pieces: God said, "Let there be light," and light came into being.

L.3: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.

R.3: Then God said, "Let there be light!" And light began to shine.

decisions.choice: let there be ... and there was: the command and the result use the same verb
decisions.reason: God's command "let it be" and the report "and it was" are two forms of one verb, so the report repeats the command word for word. The pattern returns through the chapter: God speaks, and what he says happens (Psalm 33:9).

decisions.choice: light before the sun: light is made on the first day, the sun on the fourth
alternatives: the light of the sun, coming through for the first time
decisions.reason: The sun, moon and stars are not made until verses 14-19. The account presents light as God's first work, coming from his word, not from the lights in the sky; they are later given the task of carrying it. Later scripture speaks of God himself as light (Psalm 104:2; Isaiah 60:19), and Paul recalls this verse: "Let light shine out of darkness" (2 Corinthians 4:6).

decisions.choice: light came into being (B); light began to shine (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "and there was light", which repeats the command as the Hebrew does (m1). Balanced and Readable say what happened in a verb of their own.

records.source: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָא֖וֹר כִּי־ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: And saw God the light, that [it was] good, and separated God between the light and between the darkness.
pieces: God saw that the light was good, and God divided the light from the darkness.

L.4: And God saw the light, that [it was] good, and God separated between the light and the darkness.

R.4: God saw that the light was good. He divided the light from the darkness.

decisions.choice: good: as it should be, fit for its purpose and pleasing to God
decisions.reason: The word covers what is pleasant, useful and right. Here it is God's verdict that what he has made is as it should be. The verdict comes seven times in the chapter, the last time "very good" (verse 31).

decisions.choice: separated: God divides one thing from another and so gives the world its order
decisions.reason: Separating is a key act of the first days: light from darkness, the waters above from the waters below (verse 7), day from night (verse 14). Each separation sets a boundary, and the boundaries make the world a place where life can live.

decisions.choice: saw the light, that [it was] good
alternatives: saw that the light was good
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, in which God sees the light and then judges it good, and brackets "it was", which Hebrew does not need.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And called God to the light day, and to the darkness he called night. And was evening and was morning, day one.
pieces: God named the light Day, and the darkness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Night. Evening came, and then morning: the first day.

L.5: And God called the light Day, and the darkness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, day one.

R.5: God gave the light the name Day, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the darkness the name Night. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the first day.

decisions.choice: called: naming as a sign of authority
decisions.reason: In the Bible the one who gives a name has authority over what is named. God names day and night, the sky (verse 8), and the land and the seas (verse 10); later he lets the man name the animals (2:19-20).

decisions.choice: day one: the first day, with a cardinal number
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the number "one" here, though it uses "second", "third" and so on for the other days. "One" can stand for "first" when counting (2:11; 8:13), so the meaning is the first day. The day is counted from evening, as Israel's days were counted from sunset.

decisions.choice: day: the daylight, and then a whole day marked by evening and morning
decisions.reason: The word has two senses in this verse: the daylight that God names, as against night, and the whole day that evening and morning complete. Each of the six days of work is marked in the same way, and the seventh is the day God rests (2:2-3), the pattern Israel's week follows (Exodus 20:11). Readers differ on how these days relate to the age of the world; the text presents them as a week.

decisions.choice: named (B); gave ... the name (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "called the light Day". Balanced and Readable say "named", which is what calling means here (m1).

decisions.choice: day one (L); the first day (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pattern "and there was ... and there was". Balanced and Readable say the same in a form that reads naturally aloud. Literal keeps the number "one" so the reader can see it; Balanced and Readable use the ordinal English expects (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said God, let be a vault in [the] midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters to waters.
pieces: God said, "Let there be a vault in the middle of the waters, to divide water from water."

L.6: And God said, "Let there be a vault in the midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters and waters."

R.6: Then God said, "Let there be a great dome in the middle of the waters. Let it keep the water below apart from the water above."

decisions.choice: vault: a solid-looking expanse, beaten out like metal, that holds back the waters above
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb for hammering metal into a thin sheet (Exodus 39:3), and Job 37:18 pictures the skies as hard as a mirror of cast metal. The vault is what we see as the sky: it holds back waters above it (verse 7), and the sun, moon and stars are set in it (verse 17). The account describes the world as it appears to someone standing on the earth.

decisions.choice: vault (L, B); great dome (R)
decisions.reason: "Firmament", from the Latin, is the old English word, but few readers know it now. "Expanse" loses the sense of something solid. "Vault", an arched ceiling, keeps both the shape and the solidity (m1); Readable uses "great dome", a plainer picture of the same thing.

decisions.choice: the water below apart from the water above
decisions.reason: Readable takes "below" and "above" from verse 7 to make clear which waters are meant.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And made God the vault, and separated between the waters which [were] from under to the vault and between the waters which [were] from above to the vault. And was so.
pieces: So God made the vault and divided the waters beneath it from the waters above it. And so it happened.

L.7: And God made the vault, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} separated between the waters that [were] under the vault and the waters that [were] above the vault. And it was so.

R.7: So God made the dome. He separated the water under the dome from the water above it. And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: the waters above the vault: water held back above the sky
decisions.reason: The account pictures water both below the vault and above it. When the flood comes, "the windows of the heavens" are opened (7:11), and Psalm 148:4 calls on "the waters above the heavens" to praise God.

decisions.choice: and it was so: what God commanded happened, exactly as he said
decisions.reason: This short report follows six of God's commands in the chapter (verses 7, 9, 11, 15, 24, 30). It confirms that his word was carried out as he spoke it.

decisions.choice: and it was so at the end of verse 7, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: and it was so at the end of verse 6 (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the chapter "and it was so" comes straight after God's command. Here the Hebrew text places it after the report of what God made; the Greek Septuagint has it at the end of verse 6 instead, in the usual place. The Hebrew, the less expected order, is followed here.

decisions.choice: And so it happened (B); And that is what happened (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "and it was so". Balanced and Readable say the same in current English.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָֽרָקִ֖יעַ שָׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שֵׁנִֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And called God to the vault heavens. And was evening and was morning, day second.
pieces: God named the vault Sky. Evening came, and then morning: the second day.

L.8: And God called the vault Heavens. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.

R.8: God gave the dome the name Sky. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the second day.

decisions.choice: heavens: here the visible sky, the vault overhead
decisions.reason: This is the word of verse 1. Here it is the name God gives the vault: the sky above the earth, where the birds fly (verse 20) and the lights are set (verse 14). Elsewhere it can also mean the place where God dwells (1 Kings 8:30).

decisions.choice: no "God saw that it was good" on the second day, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: And God saw that it was good (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has no verdict "good" on the second day; the Greek Septuagint adds it here, as on the other days. The Hebrew is followed. The work of separating the waters begun on day two is finished on day three, which has the verdict twice (verses 10 and 12).

decisions.choice: Sky
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Heavens", the word of verse 1. Balanced and Readable say "Sky", because that is what the vault is (m1), and "heaven" alone suggests to most readers the dwelling of God.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וְתֵרָאֶ֖ה הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And said God, let be gathered the waters from under the heavens to place one, and let appear the dry [land]. And was so.
pieces: Then God said, "Let the waters below the sky come together into one place, and let dry land be seen." And so it happened.

L.9: And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered to one place, and let the dry [land] appear." And it was so.

R.9: Then God said, "Let the water under the sky come together in one place, so that dry land appears." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: the dry land: ground no longer covered by water
decisions.reason: The word means simply "the dry": ground from which the water has gone. The same word is used when Israel crosses the sea "on dry ground" (Exodus 14:16), one of several echoes of this chapter in the story of the exodus.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text has no report that the waters were gathered
alternatives: a further sentence: and the water was gathered into its gatherings, and the dry land appeared (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint adds a sentence telling how the waters were gathered and the dry land appeared, as the account does after other commands. The Hebrew text does not have it and is followed here.

decisions.choice: the dry [land]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the dry"; Literal brackets the noun English needs.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לַיַּבָּשָׁה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵ֥ה הַמַּ֖יִם קָרָ֣א יַמִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And called God to the dry [land] earth, and to the gathering of the waters he called seas. And saw God that [it was] good.
pieces: God named the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Seas. And God saw that it was good.

L.10: And God called the dry [land] Earth, and the gathering of the waters {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Seas. And God saw that [it was] good.

R.10: God gave the dry land the name Earth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the water that had come together the name Seas. God saw that it was good.

decisions.choice: earth: here the land, as against the seas
decisions.reason: The word that meant the whole earth in verses 1 and 2 is here the name of the dry land. It can also mean a single country, as in "the land of Egypt" (Exodus 7:19).

decisions.choice: seas: all the gathered waters, not one particular sea
decisions.reason: The plural takes in every body of water: the "one place" of verse 9, seen as many seas.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תַּֽדְשֵׁ֤א הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ דֶּ֔שֶׁא עֵ֚שֶׂב מַזְרִ֣יעַ זֶ֔רַע עֵ֣ץ פְּרִ֞י עֹ֤שֶׂה פְּרִי֙ לְמִינ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And said God, let sprout the earth vegetation, plant[s] seeding seed, tree[s] of fruit making fruit to its kind, which its seed [is] in it, on the earth. And was so.
pieces: Then God said, "Let the earth put forth green growth: plants that produce seed, and trees on the earth that bear fruit with its seed inside, each according to its kind." And so it happened.

L.11: And God said, "Let the earth sprout vegetation: plants yielding seed, [and] fruit trees bearing fruit according to its kind, with its seed in it, on the earth." And it was so.

R.11: Then God said, "Let plants grow on the land: plants that make seeds, and trees with fruit that has seeds in it, each of its own kind." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: let the earth sprout: the earth brings forth at God's command
decisions.reason: God speaks to the earth, and it brings forth (verse 12), as the waters do in verse 20 and the earth again in verse 24. The power is in God's word; the earth is the means.

decisions.choice: vegetation, plants and trees: green growth in general, then its two main kinds
decisions.reason: The first word covers all fresh green growth. The two that follow name its main kinds as they are seen: plants that carry their seed openly, such as grain and herbs, and trees whose seed is inside the fruit. This is a description of what is seen, not a full botany.

decisions.choice: according to its kind: each kind producing more of its own kind
decisions.reason: The phrase comes ten times in the chapter (verses 11, 12, 21, 24, 25). Each kind of plant and animal reproduces its own kind through its seed, so that the life God has made goes on from generation to generation. The Hebrew word for kind is not a modern scientific category such as species.

decisions.choice: [and] fruit trees
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the kinds without "and"; Literal brackets the one English needs.

records.source: וַתּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ דֶּ֠שֶׁא עֵ֣שֶׂב מַזְרִ֤יעַ זֶ֨רַע֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וְעֵ֧ץ עֹֽשֶׂה־פְּרִ֛יאֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And brought forth the earth vegetation, plant[s] seeding seed to its kind, and tree[s] making fruit which its seed [is] in it to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.
pieces: The earth brought forth green growth: plants that produce seed, each according to its kind, and trees that bear fruit with its seed inside, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

L.12: And the earth brought forth vegetation, plants yielding seed according to their kind, and trees bearing fruit with its seed in it according to their kind. And God saw that [it was] good.

R.12: So the land grew plants that made seeds, and trees with fruit that had seeds in it, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.

decisions.choice: the earth brought forth: the report repeats the command
decisions.reason: The report repeats God's command in almost the same words, with "brought forth" for "sprout". The trees are no longer said to be "on the earth", and "according to its kind" is now said of the plants as well.

decisions.choice: according to their kind
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "its kind", of each plant and tree; Literal says "their", since English refers to "plants" and "trees" in the plural.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שְׁלִישִֽׁי׃פ
records.gloss: And was evening and was morning, day third.
pieces: Evening came, and then morning: the third day.

L.13: And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.

R.13: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the third day.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַיּ֖וֹם וּבֵ֣ין הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָי֤וּ לְאֹתֹת֙ וּלְמ֣וֹעֲדִ֔ים וּלְיָמִ֖ים וְשָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said God, let be lights in [the] vault of the heavens to separate between the day and between the night, and they will be for signs and for appointed times and for days and years,
pieces: Then God said, "Let there be lights in the vault of the sky to divide the day from the night. Let them be signs that mark the appointed times, the days and the years,

L.14: And God said, "Let there be lights in the vault of the heavens to separate between the day and the night, and let them be for signs and for appointed times and for days and years,

R.14: Then God said, "Let there be lights in the dome of the sky to divide the day from the night. They will show when the special times of the year come, and they will mark the days and the years.

decisions.choice: lights: lamps, things that give light
decisions.reason: The word is not "light" itself (verse 3) but a holder or source of light, a lamp; it is used for the lampstand in the tabernacle (Exodus 35:14). The lights do not make the light of day; they carry it and rule over it.

decisions.choice: signs that mark appointed times, days and years
alternatives: signs, seasons, days and years: four separate purposes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins four things with "and". They can be four separate purposes, or "signs" can be the main one and the rest what the signs mark. The second fits the sentence better: the lights are the signs by which people know the appointed times and count the days and the years.

decisions.choice: appointed times: the set times of the year, including the festivals
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed time or an appointed meeting, and it is used for Israel's festivals (Leviticus 23:2, 4). The moon and the sun set the calendar by which those times were kept (Psalm 104:19).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (L, B)
decisions.reason: God's command runs on into verse 15. Literal and Balanced keep it as one sentence, so this verse ends with a comma; Readable ends the sentence here.

records.source: וְהָי֤וּ לִמְאוֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: and they will be for lights in [the] vault of the heavens to give light on the earth. And was so.
pieces: and let them shine in the vault of the sky to give light to the earth." And so it happened.

L.15: and let them be for lights in the vault of the heavens to give light on the earth." And it was so.

R.15: Let them shine from the sky to give light to the earth." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: let them shine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "let them be for lights", with the word for lamps (verse 14). Balanced and Readable say what being a lamp means: to shine.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַמְּאֹרֹ֖ת הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים אֶת־הַמָּא֤וֹר הַגָּדֹל֙ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת־הַמָּא֤וֹר הַקָּטֹן֙ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְאֵ֖ת הַכּוֹכָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And made God the two of the lights the great, the light the great for [the] rule of the day and the light the small for [the] rule of the night, and the stars.
pieces: God made the two great lights, the larger to rule the day and the smaller to rule the night. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the stars.

L.16: And God made the two great lights, the great light for ruling the day and the small light for ruling the night, and the stars.

R.16: God made two great lights: the bigger one, the sun, to rule the day, and the smaller one, the moon, to rule the night. He also made the stars.

decisions.choice: the great light and the small light: the sun and the moon, left unnamed
decisions.reason: The account does not use the ordinary words for sun and moon, which were also the names of gods worshiped by Israel's neighbors. They are simply lights that God makes and puts in place, with a task to do. Deuteronomy 4:19 warns Israel not to worship the sun, moon and stars, which God has given to all peoples.

decisions.choice: rule: to govern, to have charge of
decisions.reason: The lights are given rule over day and night: they mark and govern the times. Rule over the living creatures is later given to human beings (verses 26 and 28), with a different verb.

decisions.choice: and the stars: added in passing
decisions.reason: The stars are added at the end, with no task of their own, the briefest mention of anything made in the chapter. Elsewhere God counts and names them (Psalm 147:4; Isaiah 40:26).

decisions.choice: great ... small (L); larger ... smaller (B); bigger ... smaller (R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no separate form for comparing two things: "the great light" and "the small light" mean the larger and the smaller of the two. Literal keeps the plain words; Balanced and Readable compare.

decisions.choice: the sun ... the moon
alternatives: the bigger one ... the smaller one
decisions.reason: Readable names the two lights so that young readers know what is meant, though the Hebrew leaves them unnamed on purpose (m1).

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And set them God in [the] vault of the heavens to give light on the earth,
pieces: God placed them in the vault of the sky to give light to the earth,

L.17: And God set them in the vault of the heavens to give light on the earth,

R.17: God put them in the sky to give light to the earth,

decisions.choice: set: put in place
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for "give". With a place it means to put or set something there, as God sets his bow in the cloud in 9:13.

records.source: וְלִמְשֹׁל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה וּֽלֲהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate between the light and between the darkness. And saw God that [it was] good.
pieces: to rule over the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

L.18: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate between the light and the darkness. And God saw that [it was] good.

R.18: to rule over the day and the night, and to keep the light apart from the darkness. God saw that it was good.

decisions.choice: to separate the light from the darkness: the lights take up the work of day one
decisions.reason: On the first day God himself separated the light from the darkness (verse 4). Now he gives that task to the lights he has made. Days one and four belong together, as do days two and five, and days three and six: the first three days shape the world, and the last three fill it.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם רְבִיעִֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And was evening and was morning, day fourth.
pieces: Evening came, and then morning: the fourth day.

L.19: And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

R.19: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the fourth day.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said God, let swarm the waters swarm[s] of living creature[s], and bird[s] let fly over the earth on [the] face of [the] vault of the heavens.
pieces: Then God said, "Let the waters teem with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the vault of the sky."

L.20: And God said, "Let the waters swarm [with] swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the vault of the heavens."

R.20: Then God said, "Let the water be full of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the sky."

decisions.choice: living creatures: beings that breathe and live
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" means a living, breathing being, or the life within it. The same words describe these animals and, in 2:7, the man ("a living being"). They do not set human beings apart from animals; what sets them apart is the image of God (verses 26-27).

decisions.choice: swarm: move in great numbers
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun both picture crowds of small creatures moving together, like shoals of fish. The waters are to teem with life.

decisions.choice: birds: flying creatures in general
decisions.reason: The word means any creature that flies, and comes from the verb "fly" in the same verse; elsewhere it includes winged insects (Leviticus 11:20). Here it is chiefly birds.

decisions.choice: swarm [with] swarms
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the root as verb and object; Literal brackets the "with" English needs.

records.source: וַיִּבְרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־הַתַּנִּינִ֖ם הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּ֣ה׀הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ע֤וֹף כָּנָף֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And created God the sea monsters the great, and every living creature the moving which swarmed the waters to their kind, and every bird of wing to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.
pieces: So God created the great sea creatures and every kind of living thing that moves and teems in the waters, and every kind of winged bird. And God saw that it was good.

L.21: And God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kind, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that [it was] good.

R.21: So God created the great creatures of the sea, and all the kinds of living things that swim in the water, and all the kinds of birds. God saw that it was good.

decisions.choice: great sea creatures: the large animals of the sea
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the same word can name a snake (Exodus 7:9) or, in poetry, a sea monster that pictures powers opposed to God (Psalm 74:13; Isaiah 27:1). Here such creatures are simply part of what God has made, and they are good.

decisions.choice: created: the verb of verse 1, used again as animal life begins
decisions.reason: The verb used only of God appears here for the first time since verse 1, as the first living creatures are made. It comes again for human beings (verse 27).

decisions.choice: moves: creeps or glides, of creatures close to the ground or in the water
decisions.reason: The verb is used for small animals that move along the ground (verse 26), and here for the creatures that move through the water.

decisions.choice: every kind of
alternatives: according to their kind ... according to its kind
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable fold "according to its kind" into "every kind of" to keep a long list readable.

records.source: וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ אֹתָ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר פְּר֣וּ וּרְב֗וּ וּמִלְא֤וּ אֶת־הַמַּ֨יִם֙ בַּיַּמִּ֔ים וְהָע֖וֹף יִ֥רֶב בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And blessed them God, saying, be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and the bird[s] let multiply on the earth.
pieces: God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters of the seas; and let the birds multiply across the earth."

L.22: And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth."

R.22: God blessed them and said, "Have many young ones. Fill the water in the seas. And let there be more and more birds on the earth."

decisions.choice: blessed: God gives them life and the power to increase
decisions.reason: To bless here is to give the gift of fruitfulness: God's blessing is the power to have young and to multiply. It is given to the sea creatures and birds, and then, in nearly the same words, to human beings (verse 28).

decisions.choice: Have many young ones
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "be fruitful and multiply" means for animals.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם חֲמִישִֽׁי׃פ
records.gloss: And was evening and was morning, day fifth.
pieces: Evening came, and then morning: the fifth day.

L.23: And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

R.23: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the fifth day.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ נֶ֤פֶשׁ חַיָּה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ בְּהֵמָ֥ה וָרֶ֛מֶשׂ וְחַֽיְתוֹ־אֶ֖רֶץ לְמִינָ֑הּ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And said God, let bring forth the earth living creature[s] to its kind, livestock and creeping thing[s] and animal[s] of earth to its kind. And was so.
pieces: Then God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures, each according to its kind: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals, each according to its kind." And so it happened.

L.24: And God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: livestock and creeping things and animals of [the] earth according to their kind." And it was so.

R.24: Then God said, "Let the land be filled with living creatures of every kind: farm animals, small creatures that crawl, and wild animals." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: livestock, creeping things and wild animals: the three groups of land animals
decisions.reason: The first word is used for the larger animals that people keep, such as cattle and sheep; the second for small animals that move close to the ground, including reptiles and insects; the third, "the living things of the earth", for wild animals. As with the plants, these are groups as people see them, not a scientific list.

decisions.choice: farm animals; small creatures that crawl
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the first two groups (m1).

records.heading: Living creatures and human beings

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֩ אֶת־חַיַּ֨ת הָאָ֜רֶץ לְמִינָ֗הּ וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And made God [the] animal[s] of the earth to its kind and the livestock to its kind and every creeping thing of the ground to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.
pieces: God made the wild animals, each according to its kind, the livestock according to their kinds, and every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

L.25: And God made the animals of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind. And God saw that [it was] good.

R.25: So God made all the kinds of wild animals, farm animals and small creatures that crawl on the ground. God saw that it was good.

decisions.choice: ground: the soil, the earth that is worked
decisions.reason: For the first time the account uses a second word for the earth: the ground, the soil that people work. It sounds like the word for the human being (adam) in the next verse, a link the story makes plain in 2:7, where God forms the man from the dust of the ground.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ וְיִרְדּוּ֩ בִדְגַ֨ת הַיָּ֜ם וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבְכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And said God, let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] bird[s] of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.
pieces: Then God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:human beings|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, to be like {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}. Let them rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the earth, and over every creature that moves along the ground."

L.26: And God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:humankind|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, according to {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth."

R.26: Then God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:people|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, to be like {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}. They will be in charge of the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, the farm animals, the whole earth, and all the small creatures that crawl on the ground."

decisions.choice: let us: God speaks in the plural as he makes human beings
alternatives: God speaks to the heavenly beings around him
a plural of fullness or majesty
a first hint of more than one person in God
decisions.reason: Until now God has said "let there be". Here he speaks in the plural, and the next verse returns to the singular ("he created"). The plural has been read in several ways: God speaking to the heavenly beings who serve him (as in 1 Kings 22:19-20, and Isaiah 6:8, "who will go for us?"), a plural that expresses God's fullness, or God deliberating with himself. Christian readers have also seen in it a first hint of the Trinity, since the New Testament links the Son with creation (John 1:3). The text itself is clear that God alone creates (verse 27).

decisions.choice: humankind: human beings, male and female, not one man
decisions.reason: Adam is the Hebrew word for human beings in general; it becomes a personal name only later in the story (4:25; 5:1-3). Here it has no article, and the words that follow, "let them rule", and verse 27, "male and female", show that it means humankind as a whole.

decisions.choice: image and likeness: human beings resemble God and represent him
alternatives: two different things in the human being, such as body and soul
decisions.reason: An image is a statue or copy, and kings of the ancient world set up images of themselves to show where they ruled. A likeness is a resemblance. Together the two words say that human beings are made to resemble God and to represent him on the earth, which is why the next words give them rule over it. The same pair is used, in the other order, when Adam fathers a son "in his likeness, according to his image" (5:3).

decisions.choice: rule: govern, as a king rules
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a king's rule (1 Kings 5:4; Psalm 72:8). Human beings are to rule the living creatures as God's representatives, and the king described in Psalm 72 rules for the good of those in his care (Psalm 72:12-14).

decisions.choice: and over all the earth, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: and over all the wild animals of the earth (Syriac)
decisions.reason: In a list of animals "all the earth" stands out, and the Syriac translation reads "all the wild animals of the earth", which matches verses 24-25 and may be what was first written. The Hebrew text and the Septuagint have "all the earth", which is followed here.

decisions.choice: humankind (L), human beings (B), people (R); with the traditional setting, man
decisions.reason: The word means human beings of both sexes (m2), so the default is an inclusive word. The gender setting gives "man", the traditional English word in this sense.

decisions.choice: us, our (lowercase by default; Us, Our with the setting)
decisions.reason: God's pronouns are lowercase by default and capitalised with the setting, including "us" and "our" here, where God speaks of himself.

decisions.choice: to be like us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "according to our likeness" means (m3) in plain words.

records.source: וַיִּבְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀אֶת־הָֽאָדָם֙ בְּצַלְמ֔וֹ בְּצֶ֥לֶם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּרָ֣א אֹת֑וֹ זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה בָּרָ֥א אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And created God the humankind in his image, in [the] image of God he created him, male and female he created them.
pieces: So God created {{gender:human beings|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} image. In the image of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created {{gender:them|him}}; male and female {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created them.

L.27: And God created {{gender:humankind|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} image, in the image of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created {{gender:them|him}}; male and female {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created them.

R.27: So God created {{gender:people|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own image. He created them to be like God. He created them male and female.

decisions.choice: three lines of poetry, each with "created"
decisions.reason: The verse is three lines of verse, each with the verb used only of God. The repetition marks the making of human beings as the high point of the account. The second line turns the first round ("created ... in his image", "in the image of God ... created") to stress the image of God.

decisions.choice: him ... them: humankind is one, and also many
decisions.reason: The second line says God created "him", singular, since humankind is one whole; the third says "them", plural, male and female. Both are said of the same humankind.

decisions.choice: male and female: both sexes, equally made in God's image
decisions.reason: The words name the two sexes, as they do of the animals in 6:19. The two together are humankind, both bear the image of God, and the blessing and the task of verse 28 are given to both.

decisions.choice: them (default); him (traditional setting)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular, "him", for humankind as one whole (m2). English "it" would sound as if humans were things, so the inclusive default says "them", as the next line does; the gender setting gives the literal "him".

decisions.choice: He created them to be like God
alternatives: in the image of God he created him
decisions.reason: Readable says what being made in the image of God means for a young reader (1:26, m3), having said "in his own image" in the first sentence.

records.source: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָם֮ אֱלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֛וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְכִבְשֻׁ֑הָ וּרְד֞וּ בִּדְגַ֤ת הַיָּם֙ וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּבְכָל־חַיָּ֖ה הָֽרֹמֶ֥שֶׂת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And blessed them God, and said to them God, be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] bird[s] of the heavens and over every living thing that creeps on the earth.
pieces: God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every living creature that moves along the ground."

L.28: And God blessed them, and God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that creeps on the earth."

R.28: God blessed them and said to them, "Have children, so that there are more and more of you. Fill the earth and take charge of it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, and over every living creature that moves on the land."

decisions.choice: God said to them: the blessing is spoken to human beings directly
decisions.reason: The sea creatures and birds were blessed in the third person (verse 22). Human beings are spoken to: "God said to them". The blessing is the same, with a task added.

decisions.choice: subdue: bring under control
decisions.reason: The verb is strong: it is used for bringing a land under control (Numbers 32:22; Joshua 18:1) and for forcing people into service (Jeremiah 34:11). Here the earth is to be brought under human care and use, in a world God has just called good; in the next chapter the man is placed in the garden "to work it and keep it" (2:15).

decisions.choice: Have children, so that there are more and more of you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "be fruitful and multiply" means for people.

decisions.choice: take charge of it
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for "subdue" (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב׀זֹרֵ֣עַ זֶ֗רַע אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעֵ֛ץ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֥וֹ פְרִי־עֵ֖ץ זֹרֵ֣עַ זָ֑רַע לָכֶ֥ם יִֽהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said God, look, I give to you every plant seeding seed which [is] on [the] face of all the earth, and every tree which in it [is] fruit of tree seeding seed; to you it will be for food,
pieces: God said, "Here, I am giving you every plant that bears seed on the face of the whole earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit. They will be your food,

L.29: And God said, "Look, I give to you every plant yielding seed that [is] on the face of all the earth, and every tree that has in it fruit yielding seed; to you it will be for food,

R.29: God said, "Look! I am giving you all the plants on the whole earth that make seeds, and all the trees that have fruit with seeds in it. You can eat them.

decisions.choice: I give: a gift made in the act of speaking
decisions.reason: The verb has a completed form, used here, as often in the Bible, for an act done by the very words that announce it: by saying it, God gives it.

decisions.choice: for food: the first gift of food is plants and fruit
decisions.reason: In this account human beings and animals are given plants to eat (verses 29-30). After the flood God also gives animals as food (9:3), with a limit. The text says no more about how people or animals lived before then.

decisions.choice: Look (L, R); Here (B)
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what follows. Older English Bibles say "behold". Balanced says "here", as one does when handing something over.

records.source: וּֽלְכָל־חַיַּ֣ת הָ֠אָרֶץ וּלְכָל־ע֨וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וּלְכֹ֣ל׀רוֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה אֶת־כָּל־יֶ֥רֶק עֵ֖שֶׂב לְאָכְלָ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: and to every animal of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to every creeping [thing] on the earth which in it [is] living life, every green of plant for food. And was so.
pieces: and for every wild animal, every bird in the sky and every creature moving on the ground, for all that has life in it, the green plants will be food." And so it happened.

L.30: and to every animal of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to every [thing] that creeps on the earth, in which [there is] living life, [I give] every green plant for food." And it was so.

R.30: And all the wild animals, the birds in the sky, and the small creatures that crawl on the ground, every living thing, can eat the green plants." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: every green plant for food: the verb carries over from verse 29
decisions.reason: This part of God's words has no verb of its own; "I give" carries over from verse 29.

decisions.choice: living life: the breath of life that animals have
decisions.reason: These are the words for "living creatures" in verses 20 and 24, used here of the life within the animals.

decisions.choice: [thing], [there is], [I give]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs that the Hebrew leaves to be understood (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־ט֖וֹב מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּֽׁי׃פ
records.gloss: And saw God all that he had made, and look, good very. And was evening and was morning, day the sixth.
pieces: God looked at everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and it was very good indeed. Evening came, and then morning: the sixth day.

L.31: And God saw all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and look, [it was] very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.

R.31: God looked at everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and it was very good. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the sixth day.

decisions.choice: and look, very good: the reader sees it with God
decisions.reason: The word "look" lets the reader see what God sees. This is the seventh time God sees that what he has made is good, and the only time the verdict is "very good": creation, with human beings in it, is complete and as it should be.

decisions.choice: the sixth day: the first of the days to have "the"
decisions.reason: Days two to five are "a second day", "a third day" and so on, without the article. The sixth day has it, as does the seventh (2:2-3), setting these days apart as the high point and the close of the week.

decisions.choice: a second day ... the sixth day (L); the second day ... the sixth day (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Hebrew: "a second day" and so on, then "the sixth day" (m2). Balanced and Readable say "the second day" and so on, as English counts.

decisions.choice: very good indeed
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "indeed" to give "very" the weight it has at the end of the verdicts (m1).
